q1.answer_given: Special-education provision is heavily shaped by staff capacity and funding: Swansea wants a dedicated educational psychologist for EOTAS learners but lacks the capacity; specialist expertise is niche and slow to rebuild when staff leave; newly qualified teachers currently can't work in EOTAS settings, and the panel wants exposure built into initial teacher training and ongoing professional development in both directions between PRU and mainstream staff, though professional development access for small EOTAS staff cohorts remains limited (improving via networks/conferences). PRU curriculum itself is broad, balanced, inspected, and satisfactory, but quality assurance and curriculum consistency weaken once learners leave the PRU system into home tuition or private provision, with regional collaboration on the new curriculum still developing.
